title: Off-Highway Vehicle (ATV / Snowmobile) Perpendicular Road Crossing Rule

no_head_on_same_lane.note: Multiple cars travel same direction in left lane; snowmobile is stopped on right shoulder, no opposing vehicles in same lane.

no_rhd_cabin.note: No car interior or steering wheel is visible; only exteriors through windshields.

single_bulb_signal.note: No traffic signal appears in the winter rural scene.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: Double-yellow centerline in middle, white edge line on right; oncoming cars use left side of center toward camera, correct for US right-hand traffic.

zero_text.note: License plates are blank white shapes, roadside marker is blank orange rectangle, no letters or numbers visible.

scene_match.note: Snowmobile stopped at snowy roadside yielding to highway cars matches, but vehicle is aligned roughly parallel to road, not turned to a clean 90-degree crossing angle.

result.summary: Snowy yield scene is correct but snowmobile alignment does not demonstrate the required 90-degree perpendicular crossing.

teaching_correct.note: Shows stopping and yielding correctly, but parallel shoulder positioning fails to model the perpendicular crossing rule and could suggest riding along road.

result.what_i_see: A helmeted rider on a snowmobile waits stopped in snow on the right shoulder of a snowy two-lane highway while three cars approach in the oncoming lane at sunset with mountains behind.
